rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, Tables 1-3, Figs 6-8 <U+2014> the authors report their own laboratory column experiments on compacted silty sand amended with 5-10% water hyacinth biochar, mesquite biochar and coir pith, measuring soil water retention curves, mini-disk infiltrometer infiltration rates and desiccation crack intensity factor.
rows.notes: The study has nothing to do with drip or sprinkler irrigation, crop yield or water productivity. It is a geotechnical laboratory study of biochar-amended compacted soil (water retention, infiltration, cracking) intended for bioengineered structures such as landfill covers and slopes; no crops were grown and no irrigation systems were compared. The passage's attribution (drip increased yield and water productivity more than sprinkler) is not supported by any result in this paper; the citation appears misattributed to a different Hussain et al. (2020). Technology mismatch flagged because the tested intervention (biochar soil amendment) differs from the claimed one (drip irrigation).

notes: Full text appears complete. The cited study (Hussain et al. 2020, Biochar 2:465-478) concerns biochar type effects on infiltration, water retention and desiccation cracking of a compacted silty sand in laboratory columns; it contains no data on drip or sprinkler irrigation, crop yield or water productivity, so the claim cannot be supported by it.
